Moladah
MOH-luh-dah
proper noun
Hebrew Moladah, perhaps “birth” or “generation,” a town of the Negeb in the south of Judah.

📖 Biblical Definition

Moladah was a town in the uttermost south of Judah, named among the cities “toward the coast of Edom southward” in the great catalogue of Judah’s inheritance (Jos 15:21, 26). When the lot of Simeon fell within the inheritance of the children of Judah, because the portion of Judah was too large for them, Moladah was reckoned among the cities given to Simeon (Jos 19:1–2). Thus it belonged to the dry southland, the Negeb, that parched and thirsty frontier where Israel learned to depend upon the LORD for wells and rain. The town does not vanish from the record after the conquest, for after the captivity the children of Judah returning from Babylon dwelt again at Moladah and the villages thereof (Neh 11:26). So the same town settled at the entrance into the land was re-inhabited by the remnant the LORD brought home, a quiet testimony that He does not forget the least-known places of His people’s heritage. Moladah, whose name may speak of birth and generation, stands as a witness that the God who gave the land also keeps it, settling Simeon safely within Judah and bringing His people back to their old borders after the long affliction of exile.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town in the south of Judah, given to Simeon, and re-inhabited by the remnant after the captivity.

expand to see more

MOLADAH, a town in the uttermost south of Judah (Jos 15:26).

It was reckoned among the cities given to Simeon within Judah (Jos 19:2).

It lay in the Negeb, the dry southland toward the coast of Edom.

The remnant returning from Babylon dwelt there again (Neh 11:26).

Its name may signify “birth” or “generation.”

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 15:26 — "Amam, and Shema, and Moladah,"

Jos 19:2 — "And they had in their inheritance Beersheba, or Sheba, and Moladah,"

Neh 11:26 — "And at Jeshua, and at Moladah, and at Beth-phelet,"

Jos 19:1 — "And the second lot came forth to Simeon, even for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families: and their inheritance was within the inheritance of the children of Judah."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses that God keeps the least-known towns of His people’s heritage.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God settled Simeon safely within Judah and remembers the least-known towns of His people’s inheritance. Moladah lay in the parched southland, where Israel learned to depend upon the LORD for wells and rain; yet it was no forgotten place, for after the long affliction of exile the remnant returned and dwelt there again. The God who gives the land also keeps it, and no quiet town of His heritage falls outside His care.

Moladah’s re-inhabiting after the captivity is a small but steady sign of the faithfulness of God to His promises. He scattered His people for their sins, yet He brought them home to their old borders, settling them once more in the towns their fathers had received by lot. The LORD does not abandon the places He has given; He restores His people to their heritage, that the praise of His covenant-keeping might rise even from the obscure villages of the Negeb.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name may mean “birth” or “generation,” borne by a town of the southland.

expand to see more

Moladah — Hebrew Moladah, perhaps “birth” or “generation.”

It lay in the uttermost south of Judah, in the Negeb.

It was reckoned among the cities given to Simeon.

It stood near Beersheba on the dry frontier.

The remnant from Babylon dwelt there again after the exile.
